## Exercise complete — welcome to the open-source journey! 🥳

You completed all four missions in the GDGoC VTU GitHub Bootcamp.

### Your accomplishments

- Created a branch.
- Created a Markdown file and committed it.
- Opened a pull request and reviewed its diff.
- Merged your pull request.
- Saw how GitHub Actions can automatically check work and guide a learner.

### Important concepts to remember

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Codebase | The source code that implements a software project |
| Repository | A project space containing files and Git history |
| README | The introduction to a repository |
| Markdown | Lightweight syntax for formatting text |
| Branch | An independent line of development |
| Commit | A recorded snapshot of staged changes |
| Pull request | A proposal to merge changes from one branch into another |
| Merge | Integrate changes into the target branch |
| Issue | A place to track work, questions, and bugs |
| GitHub Actions | Automation triggered by repository events or schedules |

### What's next?

1. **Build your profile README.** Create a public repository whose name exactly matches your GitHub username and add a non-empty `README.md` in its root. GitHub can display it at the top of your profile.
2. **Learn Git in the terminal.** Open `docs/GIT-CHEATSHEET.md` in the Code tab and practise clone, status, add, commit, branch, push, and pull.
3. **Contribute to GDGoC.** Open `COMMUNITY-CHALLENGE.md` in the Code tab to propose a real contribution to the community repository.
4. **Explore GitHub Skills.** Visit https://skills.github.com/ for more guided learning.

### About GitHub Achievements

GitHub may award profile achievements for qualifying activity. Examples include Quickdraw, Pull Shark, Pair Extraordinaire, Galaxy Brain, and Starstruck. These have their own eligibility rules and are **not guaranteed** by completing this workshop. Do not create artificial activity just to collect badges. Learn the criteria at https://docs.github.com/en/account-and-profile/reference/profile-reference#earning-achievements.

> Your bootcamp completion is a workshop milestone, not an official GitHub certification or GitHub Achievement.

**Learn. Build. Contribute. Belong.**
